symbols.name: NonExecutiveAsk
symbols.sig: export function NonExecutiveAsk({ name, ticket, busy, onYes, onNo }: { name: string; ticket: string; busy: boolean; onYes: () => void; onNo: () => void })

params.name: { name, ticket, busy, onYes, onNo }
params.type: { name: string; ticket: string; busy: boolean; onYes: () => void; onNo: () => void }

symbols.name: NonExecutiveChip
doc: I use this chip to mark a non-executive in the list of authorised people.

symbols.name: NONEXEC_ROW
doc: The look of the row of a non-executive in a list: amber instead of white.

behaviours: the question is an alert, in RED, that names the person and his ticket and asks 'Are you sure you want to authorise a non-executive?'
it has a TICK (Yes, authorise) and a CROSS (No), each with its own mark, as buttons that do not submit anything
both buttons are off while a request is on its way
what it prints is escaped (a tag in a name is text)
the chip says 'Non-executive', in amber, with its mark
the row look is amber (not the white of an executive's row)
the parts keep no state and make no request (they only draw, and call what they are given)
employee panel: a non-executive found by ticket opens the question (not a direct authorise); only the tick sends the confirmation; the cross closes it; a withdrawal clears it
employee panel: the list marks a non-executive (amber row, chip) and an unknown ticket gets the red sentence
PAX panel: the same rules (question first, tick sends the confirmation, cross closes, amber row and chip, red sentence for an unknown ticket)
PAX person row: amber and a chip for a non-executive, white for an executive (the question sits under the row)
both panels show the help text that says a non-executive needs the HOD's confirmation
